questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Infer dimensions and view placement from a stated projection convention.
questions.prompt: A crate is 90 mm wide, 54 mm deep and 32 mm high. Its front elevation shows the wide face. Which two overall dimensions should its right-end elevation show?
options: 90 mm by 54 mm
54 mm by 32 mm
90 mm by 32 mm
54 mm by 90 mm
questions.answer: 54 mm by 32 mm
questions.explanation: The end view shows the depth horizontally and the height vertically.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Infer dimensions and view placement from a stated projection convention.
questions.prompt: A drawing uses first-angle projection. Where should the view seen from the right be placed relative to the front elevation?
options: To its right.
Immediately above it.
To its left.
Immediately below it.
questions.answer: To its left.
questions.explanation: In first-angle projection the right-end view is placed on the opposite side of the front view.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Infer dimensions and view placement from a stated projection convention.
questions.prompt: A vertical groove runs down the left side of a rectangular block. A pupil aligns its plan with the front elevation, but the two views show different overall widths at the same scale. What is the most direct correction?
options: Make the plan as tall as the front elevation.
Change the scale of the front elevation alone.
Erase the groove from both views.
Project the left and right outer edges from one view to the other.
questions.answer: Project the left and right outer edges from one view to the other.
questions.explanation: Aligned plan and front views share the same overall width.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Infer dimensions and view placement from a stated projection convention.
questions.prompt: An object has the same front elevation as a rectangular block. A recess opens only on its top and stops before reaching any side. Which additional view most directly shows the shape of the recess opening?
options: Plan.
Left-end elevation.
Right-end elevation.
Bottom view.
questions.answer: Plan.
questions.explanation: The opening faces upwards and is directly visible in the plan.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret axis directions and the appearance of features in an isometric drawing.
questions.prompt: A circular inspection opening lies on the top face of a box drawn isometrically. How should the opening normally appear on the drawing?
options: As an unchanged circle.
As a straight line parallel to a vertical edge.
As an ellipse in the plane of the top face.
As a rectangle aligned with the side face.
questions.answer: As an ellipse in the plane of the top face.
questions.explanation: An isometric view foreshortens directions in the plane of the circle, making its outline elliptical.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret axis directions and the appearance of features in an isometric drawing.
questions.prompt: A pupil draws two parallel horizontal depth edges of an isometric workbench converging towards a distant point. Which change would correct the construction?
options: Make both edges vertical.
Make the farther edge disappear.
Curve both edges to meet at the same point.
Make the edges parallel to the same receding isometric axis.
questions.answer: Make the edges parallel to the same receding isometric axis.
questions.explanation: Parallel edges remain parallel in an isometric drawing.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret axis directions and the appearance of features in an isometric drawing.
questions.prompt: A sloping edge joins a marked point on the front face to a marked point on the top face of an isometric block. The edge is not parallel to any isometric axis. How should its length and direction be established?
options: Locate both endpoints and join them.
Measure its true length along the nearest axis.
Give it the same slope as the longest edge.
Draw it at 30 degrees regardless of the endpoints.
questions.answer: Locate both endpoints and join them.
questions.explanation: Non-isometric edges are located by their endpoints rather than by setting a true length along an axis.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret axis directions and the appearance of features in an isometric drawing.
questions.prompt: A rectangular frame is being drawn on the vertical left face of an isometric cabinet. Which lines should the frame's upright sides follow?

Vertical lines.
Lines converging towards the centre of the page.
Lines parallel to the top edge of the frame.
questions.answer: Vertical lines.
questions.explanation: Upright edges remain vertical in the stated isometric orientation.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a section by distinguishing cut material, voids and parts beyond the plane.
questions.prompt: A cutting plane passes through two wooden walls and the empty gap between them. Which region should remain clear of section hatching?
options: The first wall only.
The second wall only.
Both cut walls.
The empty gap.
questions.answer: The empty gap.
questions.explanation: Hatching represents solid material cut by the plane. The gap contains no material.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a section by distinguishing cut material, voids and parts beyond the plane.
questions.prompt: Two different solid parts touch along a boundary in an assembly section. Both are cut by the plane. How can their cut surfaces be distinguished?
options: Keep the boundary and vary the hatching direction or spacing between parts.
Hatch across the boundary as if the parts were one solid.
Remove the boundary and leave both parts blank.
Fill both surfaces with the same solid black tone.
questions.answer: Keep the boundary and vary the hatching direction or spacing between parts.
questions.explanation: A visible boundary and contrasting hatching help a reader distinguish adjoining components.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a section by distinguishing cut material, voids and parts beyond the plane.
questions.prompt: A sectional view shows a solid lug behind the cutting plane. The plane does not intersect the lug, but the lug is visible in the viewing direction. How should the lug be represented?
options: Hatch its entire face like a cut surface.
Show its visible outline without section hatching.
Omit it solely because it is behind the plane.
Use hatching instead of an outline.
questions.answer: Show its visible outline without section hatching.
questions.explanation: Visible features beyond the plane may be outlined. Hatching identifies the material actually intersected.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Technical Drawing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a section by distinguishing cut material, voids and parts beyond the plane.
questions.prompt: Two arrows on a labelled cutting-plane line point towards the rear of a component. What information do the arrows supply?
options: The pitch of the hatch lines.
The depth of every recess.
The direction from which the section is viewed.
The order in which parts are assembled.
questions.answer: The direction from which the section is viewed.
questions.explanation: Cutting-plane arrows indicate viewing direction. The line itself locates the cut.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Interpret how tonal relationships describe an observed object and its contact with a surface.
questions.prompt: A round clay pot has a clear highlight and a shadowed side. The drawing shades the whole pot uniformly. Which revision would most directly suggest its volume?
options: Vary the tone across the pot to match the observed light and shade.
Draw the outline more heavily on every side.
Darken the background to the same tone as the pot.
Enlarge the pot while retaining the uniform shading.
questions.answer: Vary the tone across the pot to match the observed light and shade.
questions.explanation: Tonal change across a curved surface helps the viewer perceive its volume.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Interpret how tonal relationships describe an observed object and its contact with a surface.
questions.prompt: A lamp is placed at the front left of a single object on a table. In which general direction should the object's cast shadow extend across the table?
options: Towards the lamp at the front left.
Away from the lamp towards the back right.
Vertically upwards from the table.
Towards the front right regardless of the lamp.
questions.answer: Away from the lamp towards the back right.
questions.explanation: The object blocks light along rays travelling away from the source, so the shadow extends to the opposite side.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Interpret how tonal relationships describe an observed object and its contact with a surface.
questions.prompt: A drawing shows a wooden block's shadow beginning well away from its base, although the block rests flat on the table in the arrangement. What should the artist check first?
options: Whether the page should be turned sideways.
Whether the block is larger than the page.
Whether the observed shadow meets the base where it contacts the table.
Whether the background is the same colour as the block.
questions.answer: Whether the observed shadow meets the base where it contacts the table.
questions.explanation: Correctly representing the contact between object and shadow helps ground it on the surface.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Interpret how tonal relationships describe an observed object and its contact with a surface.
questions.prompt: A pupil wants to keep a pale reflection on a dark glazed jug visible in a graphite study. Which approach best preserves that effect?
options: Make the entire jug the darkest tone.
Draw a separate outline around every shaded patch.
Erase all tones from the jug.
Leave or lift a lighter area at the observed reflection and deepen the tones around it.
questions.answer: Leave or lift a lighter area at the observed reflection and deepen the tones around it.
questions.explanation: Local tonal contrast can make the lighter reflection visible while preserving the dark surface.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose how framing, proportion and overlapping contours affect an observational drawing.
questions.prompt: From the artist's seat, a short tin hides the lower corner of a tall carton. How should the carton's edge be drawn at the overlap?
options: Continue the edge visibly across the front of the tin.
End the visible part of the edge where it meets the tin.
Erase the whole carton outline.
Make the tin transparent with crosshatching.
questions.answer: End the visible part of the edge where it meets the tin.
questions.explanation: A nearer opaque object interrupts the visible contours behind it.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one mark are author practice choices. Paper III is listed as objective, with topic allocation and official item details unverified.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose how framing, proportion and overlapping contours affect an observational drawing.
questions.prompt: A sketch of three objects matches their sizes relative to each other, but the group occupies only a tiny corner of a large blank sheet. The brief asks for a balanced use of space. Which revision addresses the problem while preserving proportion?
options: Enlarge just the nearest object until it fills the sheet.
Move one object off the page.
Enlarge the group together and plan margins around it.
Increase the outline thickness without changing placement.
questions.answer: Enlarge the group together and plan margins around it.
questions.explanation: Scaling the group as a whole keeps relative sizes intact and allows the page space to be used deliberately.

questions.prompt: A pupil holds a pencil at arm's length to compare the visible height of a jug with the width of a tray. What is the main purpose of this comparison?

To choose the light source's position.
To measure the distance from the paper to the table.
To estimate their relative sizes from the chosen viewpoint.
questions.answer: To estimate their relative sizes from the chosen viewpoint.
questions.explanation: A consistent sighting position helps transfer observed proportions to the drawing.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose how framing, proportion and overlapping contours affect an observational drawing.
questions.prompt: An artist is drawing the handle of an enamel mug. Which observation is most useful for checking the shape of the handle opening?
options: Compare the enclosed patch of background with the same patch in the observed mug.
Compare only the overall height and width of the mug.
Copy the outer handle contour and assume the opening has the same proportions.
Estimate the opening from the darkest tone on the mug.
questions.answer: Compare the enclosed patch of background with the same patch in the observed mug.
questions.explanation: The shape of the background visible through the handle provides an independent check on its inner contour.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select layout and lettering decisions that make poster information easy to find and read.
questions.prompt: A poster announcing a reading festival gives the date and organiser's name much larger lettering than the event title. Viewers often miss what the poster advertises. Which revision addresses this problem?
options: Make every line the same size as the organiser's name.
Place the event title behind a busy illustration.
Give the event title the strongest visual emphasis and group the details beneath it.
Repeat the date in the largest available space.
questions.answer: Give the event title the strongest visual emphasis and group the details beneath it.
questions.explanation: The event title should be the first message noticed. Grouping details supports the reading order.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select layout and lettering decisions that make poster information easy to find and read.
questions.prompt: A school display poster uses pale yellow lettering over a pale cream background. Which change most directly improves the lettering's visibility?
options: Reduce the spacing between every pair of letters.
Add more lines of information in the same colours.
Turn each line at a different angle.
Use a darker lettering colour that contrasts clearly with the cream.
questions.answer: Use a darker lettering colour that contrasts clearly with the cream.
questions.explanation: Greater contrast between lettering and background makes the words easier to distinguish.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select layout and lettering decisions that make poster information easy to find and read.
questions.prompt: A poster shows a single image at the top and the venue, time and admission details scattered among unrelated decorations. How could the designer help visitors locate all three details quickly?
options: Place the related details in one clearly spaced information group.
Increase the number of decorative borders.
Put the details in separate corners with identical headings.
Change each word to a different typeface.
questions.answer: Place the related details in one clearly spaced information group.
questions.explanation: Grouping related information reduces the search needed to find the practical details.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select layout and lettering decisions that make poster information easy to find and read.
questions.prompt: At a normal viewing distance, letters in a poster headline touch and several words appear to run together. Which revision should the designer try first?
options: Add a picture behind the headline.
Adjust letter spacing and restore clear spaces between words.
Use a second outline around each word.
Make all letters thinner without changing their positions.
questions.answer: Adjust letter spacing and restore clear spaces between words.
questions.explanation: Suitable letter and word spacing keeps the shapes distinct and makes the headline readable.
